en: The Apadāna of the Elder Gayākassapa Chapter on Renown (Yasavagga), Number 3 [Verse 1] When the Buddha, the Great Sage, was seated upon the seat of enlightenment, I offered him a handful of lotuses with a mind full of faith. [Verse 2] Having performed that deed of merit, I passed through many births; For eighty-four thousand aeons, I never fell into the lower realms. [Verse 3] In this fortunate aeon, during the time of Kassapa the Buddha, I was born as a human being, endowed with great renown. [Verse 4] I was known by the name Kassapa, a master of the three Vedas; I was a teacher of the Vedas, honored and highly esteemed. [Verse 5] Then, having heard of the appearance of the Buddha, the Great Sage, I went forth into homelessness under the guidance of the Tathāgata. [Verse 6] Having gone forth, I practiced the holy life with diligence; I attained the state of an Arhat, free from all defilements. [Verse 7] Today, I am the foremost among those who possess renown; By the power of that gift of flowers, I have attained this fruit. [Verse 8] May you also, O monks, practice the holy life with diligence; By means of this Dhamma, you too shall attain the deathless state.
“At that time, clad in a garment of antelope skin and carrying a load of a khāri,
having caused the khāri to be carried away, I— ”
He went to the Kola hermitage.
At that time, the Blessed One was alone,
without a second, a Conqueror.
He approached me,
illuminating all directions;
having gladdened his own mind, he—
Having paid homage to the one of excellent vows,
I took the jujube fruit with both hands and gave it to the Buddha.
In the thirty-first aeon from now,
because I gave that fruit at that time,
I do not know a state of woe.
This is the fruit of giving kola-fruit:
my defilements have been incinerated... [and so forth].
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me... [as before] ...
Thus was the Buddha’s teaching spoken:
the four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Gayākassapa recite these verses.
This is the third legend of the elder Gayākassapa.
